title: Railway Tiles & Cross-Workspace Jumpboard — persistent context prototype for fast routing
creator: Marta López
description: Problem: users lose task context when switching workspaces and the current sidebar feels modal-heavy for multi-step flows (dashboards, rollouts, cost lenses). Goal: create a lightweight, persistent rail pattern ("Railway Tiles") that surfaces destination tiles, preserves the last active context for quick returns, and exposes a cross-workspace jumpboard for keyboard and mouse discovery. This ticket captures the high-fidelity prototype, trade-offs discussed with Eng, and feedback from usability sessions.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype demonstrates persistent context pill for each workspace that stores last-opened route (dashboards/rollouts/cost)
Cross-workspace jumpboard accessible via Cmd/Ctrl+K and via a compact chevron; returns search-like results with workspace scoping
Railway Tiles respect role-based visibility (project vs org-level) and collapse gracefully on narrow viewports
Design spec includes interaction states, keyboard flows, animation timings, and a11y notes (focus order, aria labels)
Engineering accepts performance budget constraints for animations and the proposed telemetry hooks
steps_taken: Initial concept workshop with PM (Ben Carter) and Eng leads on 2025-02-06 to align IA goals
Low-fi sketches iterated into mid-fi flow with three variants: stacked rail, tile subway, and hybrid mini-rail (sketched 2025-02-11)
Built high-fi Figma prototype (link below) with two routes: Dashboard-focused and Rollout-focused workspace states
Conducted 6 moderated usability sessions (2025-02-20 to 2025-02-27). Key learnings: users expect immediate context restore and want keyboard-first access
Presented engineering trade-offs on 2025-03-03: suggested persistence via local cache + optional server flag for cross-device sync (eng prefers server flag gated behind release rollout)
Updated prototype to include cost-view micro-lens that surfaces recent cost queries as quick tiles (2025-03-09)
decisions: Use a hybrid mini-rail: tiles for top-level destinations, collapsed chevron for full rail on hover/click
Persist last-active route per workspace locally by default; enable server-backed sync as opt-in for Dedicated/Private customers
Expose jumpboard via Cmd/Ctrl+K and a small launcher on the left rail; results list grouped by workspace then route
Defer automatic model-aware context suggestions to a follow-up ticket (complexity + privacy concerns)
tradeoffs_and_risks: Local persistence is fast and simple but loses cross-device continuity for free-tier users
Aggressive animation and micro-transitions improve perceived speed but may add CPU work on low-end devices
Adding too many tiles increases rail density; prototype uses progressive reveal to avoid cognitive overload
review_feedback: PM Ben Carter: prefer default to show 'Last visited' pill for first 3 tiles, then compress older history - accepted
Eng lead Jia Nwankwo: requested an explicit telemetry event for 'jumpboard_open' and 'workspace_restore' - added to spec
Accessibility reviewer Samir Patel: ask to confirm high-contrast hover states and ensure tile selection is announced - resolved 2025-03-10
next_steps: Finalize design tokens and handoff package (target 2025-03-18)
Create ENG spike ticket to prototype persistence layer across Dedicated and Private (link: ENG-28766)
Run small A/B experiment to measure time-to-destination and retention after workspace switches (2-week pilot)
Prepare rollout plan with toggle flags: feature.disabled, feature.local_persistence, feature.server_sync
notes_for_engineering: Preferred implementation: minimal DOM footprint; use CSS transform animations rather than layout-driven transitions
Telemetry hook names and payload shapes in Confluence doc; include workspace_id and route_id when emitting 'workspace_restore'
Provide feature flag gating and a config for max tile count per rail (default 6)
